bull_bear.body: Dividend maintained at 30% (Rs. 1.50/share). Strategic conversion of Rs. 112 Cr subsidiary loans to equity to clean balance sheet and comply with regulations. Reinvestment in AI R&D and global delivery capabilities.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Government tender timing delays; Equipment price volatility (geopolitical impacts); Slow AI adoption in regulated sectors (Pharma); Execution risk on large Rs. 600 Cr+ bids; Regulatory approval timelines (RBI) for final audit clearance.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and transparent; Acknowledged past governance issues but emphasized full resolution of audit qualifications; Aggressive on AI transformation ('AI-first strategy'); Optimistic on FY27 government rebound despite Q4 softness.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'one-time' ECL provision artificially suppressed PAT while simultaneously creating a Rs. 21 Cr deferred tax asset that cushioned the bottom line; Management explicitly linked Q4 government slowdown to Iran-Israel war impacting equipment costs, causing them to walk away from specific bids rather than compete at loss-making prices; The conversion of loans to equity was framed as correcting the 'economic substance' of funds originally intended for US acquisitions.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet described as "Net Debt Free" with a Cash Reserve of Rs. 134 cr on the FY26 summary slide.
- Debt to Equity shown at 0.10, 0.09, 0.10, 0.11 and 0.11 (x) for FY22 through FY26 - i.e. persistently minimal leverage.
- Working capital has moved the wrong way on both measures the deck shows: Debtor Days 118, 84, 81, 76, 96 (FY22-FY26) and Current Ratio 4.00, 4.13, 3.58, 3.01, 2.52 (FY22-FY26).
- Returns shown are modest for an asset-light model: ROE 5%, 9%, 7%, 7%, 5% and ROCE 9%, 13%, 10%, 14%, 14% for FY22-FY26 (FY22 and FY23 marked "Exclusive of exceptional income from FY22 & loss from discontinued operations from FY23").
- The deck states no dividend policy, no buyback, no capex plan and no acquisition intent.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Self-described as "a publicly listed global leader in Information Technology consulting and services, with a legacy dating back to 1984", operating as "a trusted Managed Services Provider and Master Systems Integrator".
- Claims a first-mover position in Indian smart cities: "we became the first company to execute a Smart City project with the successful delivery of the Pune City Surveillance project in 2015"; the scale slide shows 14 Smart / Safe Cities.
- Customer-base credentials on the scale slide: 175 Number of Customers and 10 Fortune 100 Customers; a later slide instead says "We proudly partner with several Fortune 500 companies" (the deck uses both formulations).
- Service portfolio spans five stated pillars - AI Ops & Automation, Cloud Infrastructure Services, Cyber Security & Networking, Software Services and Digital Workplace Services - plus Digital Engineering Solutions (Master Systems Integration, Safe/Smart City, IBMS, IoT, command and control, image analytics).
- The Chairman frames the current phase around "integrated capabilities across managed services, digital infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity and AI-led transformation" in an environment where "macroeconomic uncertainties and evolving geopolitical developments continue to influence discretionary technology spending".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [New engagements] Entry into a new service line is claimed: an Enterprise Application Services engagement with "a leading NYSE-listed electronic design and test solutions company" covering ServiceNow, Jitterbit and Boomi, which "marks Allied Digital's entry into the Enterprise Application Services space".
- [New engagements] Other wins listed: end-to-end Workplace Services for a customer-owned (mutual) bank in Australia across Melbourne, Sydney and Adelaide; a turnkey System Integrator project from the Department of School Education, Government of Punjab for an Integrated Command and Control Centre; managed services for a Government of India organisation under the Ministry of Commerce; IT Asset Management for an international property consulting firm; and IT infrastructure support for "one of India's leading FMCG companies".
- [Renewals] "Renewed multiple strategic customer engagements across the pharmaceuticals, chemicals, real estate, BFSI, medical devices and retail design sectors" - the deck gives no contract values, durations or order book for any win or renewal.
- [FY26 one-off] The FY26 EBITDA figure of Rs. 112 cr is footnoted "* Excluding one-time provision of Rs. 36 Cr in FY26"; the deck does not say what the provision relates to.
- [Corporate history] Acquired EnPointe Global Services LLC in 2008 to expand US presence; converted to a public limited company and listed on BSE and NSE in 2007; the Chairman is described as leading the company "through Version 6.0".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Current EBITDA margin 11% pressured by one-time ECL provisions and elevated direct expenses (equipment supply up 3-4% due to project capex phases). AI-driven automation expected to reduce labor costs and lift margins to 12.5-13% in FY27. Direct expenses normalized ex-one-offs.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

Order inflow: Strong pipeline with major awards expected in Q2/Q3 FY27. Capex/Commissioning: Mumbai project (Rs. 150-200 Cr) to commission in 9 months followed by 5-year O&M.

deepdive.thesis: Allied Digital achieved record revenue (Rs. 968 Cr, +20% YoY) and resolved critical audit qualifications regarding inter-corporate loans, clearing the path for institutional confidence. Growth is pivoting toward high-margin Enterprise AI and Managed Services, with a robust Rs. 2,000 Cr+ government pipeline in Maharashtra expected to rebound in FY27 despite Q4 delays caused by geopolitical equipment cost volatility.

open.item: The Company enters FY2026-27 with a healthy pipeline of sizeable opportunities and expects several active deals to progress toward closure in the early quarters, with the pipeline strengthening through the remainder of the year as macroeconomic conditions improve by end of the second quarter.

The Board has recommended a dividend of ₹1.50 per share of ₹5 each (30% of equity share capital) for the year ended March 31, 2026, absorbing ₹847.71 lakhs of cash, payable to members on the register as on August 28, 2026.
The Company has embarked on a 10x growth strategy targeting sustained annual growth of more than 25% over the long term.
The Company is targeting ₹1,000 crore of revenue, having closed FY2025-26 at an exit run rate of ₹1,000 crore on annual revenue of ₹968 crore.

The Company has strengthened its sales and marketing engine - adding senior sales leadership in the US, expanding the sales organisation, appointing a new leader for the India managed services business and globally implementing Salesforce - initiatives expected to improve market visibility, customer engagement and conversion discipline.

The Company is augmenting advanced workflow capabilities to transform IT processes and enable autonomous virtual agents, having developed the first version of its agentic AI architecture, piloted it with selected customers, evaluated multiple AI platforms and trained more than 100 key resources in AI.

The Company continues to build strategic partnerships with leading global technology players, with IBM recently added as a strategic partner that has already contributed to a large FMCG opportunity and through which several additional opportunities are being actively pursued.

The Company is actively expanding into newer geographies - evaluating partnerships in Japan, having established new partnerships in Mauritius to address Mauritius and Africa, and continuing to explore inorganic growth opportunities globally.

open.horizon: roadmap for next three to five years; longer-term ambition
open.item: The Company has defined a clear roadmap for the next three to five years aligned with its longer-term ambition to build a business ten times its current scale.
As the business scales beyond the ₹1,000 crore annualised revenue run-rate milestone, operating leverage is expected to improve progressively.
open.promised: 1000 INR crore annualised revenue run rate

open.item: Management remains focused on progressively improving EBITDA margins from current levels (11% in FY26) towards the low to mid-teens while continuing to invest in technology, talent and long-term growth.
The Government of Maharashtra awarded the Company a five-year comprehensive safe-city project, including a command centre, for an industrial zone, to be executed over the contract period.
Expand the Company's cybersecurity consulting practice across global markets.
Acquire new customers in public-place technologies by leveraging emerging capabilities in computer vision and digital twins.
Strengthen offerings in data-centre build and infrastructure services for AI workloads.
Advance an AI-first strategy across service lines, enterprise AI, automation solutions and AI governance.
Continue geographic expansion across Japan and EMEA markets.

Digital Desk continues to be enhanced with new capabilities, the AIM 360 cybersecurity framework has been extended through an assessment platform aligned with NIST-based industry controls, and computer-vision applications are being expanded beyond smart cities into enterprise environments.

risks.note: Given its global footprint, diversified service portfolio and increasing participation in large transformation programmes, the Company is exposed to macroeconomic, geopolitical, regulatory, cybersecurity, delivery, talent and contract-management risks. Interest-rate movements, currency fluctuations, trade and tariff pressures, geopolitical conflict and energy-price volatility can influence customer spending, delivery costs and supply-chain stability across markets. Mitigated through quarterly management reviews, internal audits, proactive risk monitoring, supply-chain de-risking and operating discipline across business units.
risks.risk: Volatile global outlook - macroeconomic, geopolitical and currency exposure

risks.note: Developments in Industry 4.0, agentic AI, connected infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity and digital engineering require continuous investment in skills, platforms and delivery models - technology-led change presents both opportunity and execution risk. Mitigated through structured technology-practice plans, R&D investment across geographies, expanding AI and cybersecurity capabilities and continuous team training.
risks.risk: Technology obsolescence and execution risk from rapid technology-led change

risks.note: AI is a defining growth opportunity but organisations that scale AI without adequate controls may expose sensitive information, create operational vulnerabilities or weaken decision governance. The Company is addressing this through AI training, internal policy development, responsible solution design and a formal AI usage framework aligned with its AI-first strategy, and is refining its AI governance policy.
risks.risk: AI governance, privacy, data-security, ethical-use and accountability risk

risks.note: As the Company executes larger and more complex contracts it must protect customer environments and its own; it strengthens data protection, operational resilience, contractual safeguards and cyber-insurance coverage, supported by 24x7x365 monitoring of IT assets with leading tools, weekly security alerts and awareness checklists, controlled access and device binding, continuous patching, periodic vulnerability scanning of Digital Desk and Company websites, and continuous review of customer contracts for security obligations, risk allocation and insurance adequacy.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity - one of the most critical risks for a managed service provider

risks.note: Operating across multiple countries, non-compliance with legal, regulatory, labour, tax, data-protection and contractual requirements may result in legal exposure, financial penalties, operational disruption or reputational impact. Managed through defined ownership across sales, business units and corporate functions, periodic monitoring of regulatory changes, third-party specialists in selected jurisdictions, maintenance of certifications such as ISO, CMMI and PinkVERIFY, upgraded core platforms (SAP, Salesforce) and preparation for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
risks.risk: Compliance risk across multiple countries, including data protection

risks.note: Delivery risk arises when service commitments, quality standards, response timelines or customer expectations are not met in a highly competitive managed-services market where customers expect continuous improvement, automation-led efficiency and measurable value. Mitigated through shift-left automation, analytical dashboards, disciplined pricing, delivery governance and active service monitoring. Payment delays remain a global operational concern, with the finance team managing receivables through structured follow-up and cash-flow discipline.
risks.risk: Delivery risk and receivables / payment delays

risks.note: Risk may arise from unclear scope, changing customer expectations, complex delivery dependencies or evolving commercial terms; mitigated by standardising contract structures where appropriate, strengthening contract administration, improving understanding of customer environments and continuously refining contracts in line with service obligations and risk-allocation requirements.

As a service-centric, talent-driven organisation, the ability to attract, develop and retain specialised talent is essential to competitiveness; attrition, skill scarcity and changing workforce expectations can affect delivery continuity and cost efficiency. Mitigated through cross-training, global and domestic recruitment models, collaboration with internal and external recruiters, leadership strengthening, skill-development programmes and close delivery oversight.
risks.risk: Employee-related risk - attrition and specialised skill scarcity in a talent-driven business
